The premises lack specific prior evidence from the cited passages.
premises: Grain boundary engineering can increase the fraction of low-energy/special boundaries in stainless steel.
Low-energy grain boundaries reduce defect density and facilitate uniform passive film formation.
A uniform, low-defect passive film increases pitting breakdown potential and reduces corrosion current density.
Cyclic deformation and controlled annealing can refine the grain boundary network in nuclear-grade stainless steel.
The proposed mechanism operates under chloride-rich aqueous conditions at room temperature.
